class.name: CgameHairStrands
class.brief_description: Native strand-based hair: guide-strand physics, interpolated render strands, culling and ribbon mesh generation.
class.description: [CgameHairStrands] simulates a small number of guide strands with Verlet integration, global shape matching toward the rest pose, Dynamic Follow-The-Leader length constraints and capsule collision. Dense render strands are interpolated from each guide and its two nearest neighbours, and can be turned into a camera-facing ribbon mesh whose vertices are expanded by a vertex shader. Guide [code]g[/code] owns the points [code][g * points_per_guide, (g + 1) * points_per_guide)[/code]; point [code]0[/code] is the pinned root. Rest positions are stored in head space, simulated positions in world space, so [method step] takes the current head transform. Capsule colliders are specified in head space. Ribbon mesh vertices use these attributes: [code]NORMAL[/code] is the strand tangent, [code]UV[/code] is [code](side 0/1, t root to tip)[/code] and [code]COLOR[/code] is [code](half width, per-strand random, t, 1)[/code]. Every strand point produces two vertices at the same position. [codeblock] var hair := CgameHairStrands.new() hair.grow_guides(root_points, root_normals, 8, 0.3) hair.add_capsule(Vector3(0, 0, 0), Vector3(0, 0.1, 0), 0.12) hair.reset(head.global_transform) # Every physics frame: hair.step(delta, head.global_transform) $HairMesh.mesh = hair.build_ribbon_mesh(4, 1234, 0.002) [/codeblock] [b]Credits:[/b] Dynamic Follow-The-Leader after Müller, Kim and Chentanez, "Fast Simulation of Inextensible Hair and Fur" (VRIPHYS 2012); only the published idea is used. Shape matching, guide-to-render-strand interpolation and capsule collision follow the concepts of AMD TressFX (MIT License). The small-step XPBD family and Ten Minute Physics (Matthias Müller, MIT License) inspired the sibling [CgameXPBDCloth] and [CgameXPBDRope] classes.

method.name: add_capsule
method.description: Adds a capsule collider between points [param a] and [param b] given in head space. Strand points are kept outside [param radius] plus [member collision_margin].

method.name: build_mesh
method.description: Builds a ribbon mesh from the given strands, for example the result of [method render_strands]. Strands with fewer than two points are skipped. Returns an empty mesh when no strand is usable.

method.name: build_ribbon_mesh
method.description: Interpolates [param per_guide] render strands per guide using [param seed] and builds the ribbon mesh in one native pass, without creating the intermediate strand arrays. The result is identical to calling [method render_strands] followed by [method build_mesh].

method.name: cull
method.description: Returns the indices of guides that are visible. [param view_frustum_planes] use the [method Camera3D.get_frustum] convention: normals point outward and a point is inside when its distance to every plane is not positive. Guides farther than [member max_distance] from [param view_pos] are culled.

method.name: get_guide_count
method.description: Returns the number of guide strands.

method.name: get_neighbors
method.description: Returns the two nearest guides of every guide, two entries per guide, used for render strand interpolation.

method.name: get_points_per_guide
method.description: Returns the number of points per guide ([code]segments + 1[/code]).

method.name: get_pos
method.description: Returns the current world-space positions of all guide points.

method.name: get_prev
method.description: Returns the previous-frame world-space positions used by the Verlet integrator.

method.name: get_rest
method.description: Returns the rest positions of all guide points in head space.

method.name: get_seg_len
method.description: Returns the constant length of one guide segment.

method.name: get_segments
method.description: Returns the number of segments per guide.

method.name: grow_guides
method.description: Builds one straight guide per root along its normal, all in head space, with [param segments] segments and total [param length]. The number of guides is the smaller of the two array sizes. Neighbour links are rebuilt and the simulation must be re-initialized with [method reset] or the next [method step].

method.name: guide_points
method.description: Returns the current world-space points of the guide with the given index.

method.name: lod_strand_count
method.description: Returns how many render strands per guide to draw for a screen coverage from [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code]. Returns [code]0[/code] when the hair is too small to draw. The result never decreases with coverage and never exceeds [member max_per_guide].

method.name: render_strands
method.description: Returns [param per_guide] interpolated strands for every guide, blended from the guide and its two nearest neighbours with seeded random weights and a lateral offset of up to [member strand_spread]. Strand [code]0[/code] of each guide is the guide itself. The same [param seed] always gives the same strands.

method.name: reset
method.description: Snaps all guides to the rest pose under [param head_transform] and clears their velocity.

method.name: step
method.description: Advances the simulation by [param dt] seconds with the head at [param head_transform]. Initializes the hair first if it was not reset yet. Does nothing without guides or when [param dt] is not positive.

members.member: Extra distance, in meters, kept between strand points and capsule surfaces.
Fraction of velocity retained per frame at 60 Hz.
Fraction of the length-constraint correction that is removed from the velocity, which stops chains from whipping.
Number of Follow-The-Leader and collision iterations per step.
Guides farther than this distance from the viewer are removed by [method cull].
Global shape matching strength per frame at 60 Hz, pulling points toward the moving rest pose.
How much softer the tip is than the root: tip stiffness is [code]stiffness * (1 - bias)[/code].
Lateral jitter of interpolated render strands, in meters.
